difficultyReason: Single causal inference where the alternative explanation is explicit and ruled out by the correct answer. The argument assumes that absence of evidence is evidence of absence.
stimulus: The office break room has been unusually quiet this week. The most likely explanation is that several members of the morning coffee group have taken vacation time. However, it could also be that the office cooling system broke down, causing employees to stay at their desks rather than linger in the break room.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the argument that the quiet break room is due to vacation time rather than a broken cooling system?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The office cooling system is regularly inspected and maintained by a professional contractor.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The office break room temperature has been normal all week.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Vacation time is most commonly taken during the summer months.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The morning coffee group typically consists of five employees.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Employees have not reported any complaints about the break room this week.

explanations.correct: By confirming that the cooling system was working normally, this rules out the alternative explanation for the quiet break room. The argument asserts that vacation time is the most likely cause; showing that the competing cause (broken cooling system) did not occur strengthens the conclusion.
explanations.A: While maintenance history is mentioned, this does not confirm the system was working this particular week, so it does not rule out the break-down alternative.
explanations.B: Correct. This directly eliminates the competing cause.
explanations.C: This is about general vacation patterns and does not address whether these specific employees took time off this week.
explanations.D: Accurate but irrelevant to whether they were actually absent this week.
explanations.E: The absence of complaints is consistent with either explanation and does not strengthen the case for vacation time over a cooling problem.

difficultyReason: Straightforward medical/health causal claim. The correct answer confirms a load-bearing premise: that the mechanism actually produces the claimed effect.
stimulus: Dr. Patel observed that patients who take daily walks show improved blood pressure readings after eight weeks. She concludes that regular walking reduces high blood pressure. The effect is likely due to increased cardiovascular fitness that comes from regular aerobic exercise.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens Dr. Patel's reasoning?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Eight weeks is a sufficient period to observe measurable improvements in cardiovascular fitness from daily walking.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Some patients with high blood pressure do not benefit from medication.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Blood pressure readings can fluctuate due to stress and diet.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Walking is less strenuous than running as a form of aerobic exercise.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Patients who walk daily report feeling more relaxed.

explanations.correct: Dr. Patel's argument rests on the assumption that eight weeks is long enough for walking to produce cardiovascular improvements that then lower blood pressure. Confirming this timeline strengthens her causal chain from walking to fitness to lower blood pressure.
explanations.A: Correct. This validates the temporal component of her proposed mechanism.
explanations.B: Medication is not mentioned in her argument, so this is irrelevant.
explanations.C: While true, this introduces alternative factors but does not strengthen her walk-causation claim.
explanations.D: Walking being less intense than running does not support the claim that walking itself reduces blood pressure.
explanations.E: Feeling relaxed is a side effect, not the same as confirming the cardiovascular mechanism she proposes.

difficultyReason: Simple economic causal argument. The alternative explanation (supply reduction, not demand) is explicit; ruling it out strengthens the demand-side conclusion.
stimulus: The price of coffee has risen by 30% over the past year. This increase is likely due to increased global demand for coffee as emerging markets consume more. A competing theory suggests that the price rise is caused by poor harvests reducing supply.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most helps to support the argument that increased demand is driving the coffee price rise?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Coffee yields in major producing countries were normal or above normal this year.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The global coffee market is heavily influenced by commodity speculators.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Emerging market populations are growing faster than developed market populations.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Tea prices have also risen over the past year.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Coffee is an essential commodity in many developed countries.

explanations.correct: By showing that harvests were normal or above normal, this eliminates the supply-shortage alternative explanation. If supply was not constrained, then demand-side factors become the more plausible driver of price increases.
explanations.A: Correct. This rules out the competing supply-reduction theory.
explanations.B: Speculation might affect price but doesn't address whether demand or supply is the primary driver.
explanations.C: While relevant to emerging markets generally, this does not directly confirm increased coffee demand or rule out the supply explanation.
explanations.D: Tea price changes are independent of coffee and do not strengthen the demand argument.
explanations.E: Essential status doesn't explain why price rose this particular year or rule out supply constraints.

difficultyReason: Straightforward policy argument with a single observable alternative. Correct answer confirms that the policy mechanism works as intended.
stimulus: The state is considering raising the speed limit on rural highways from 55 to 65 mph. Traffic safety officials predict this will increase accident rates because drivers will spend less time in careful attention. However, the change might instead improve safety if it reduces the gap between posted limits and actual driving speeds.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the officials' prediction that raising the speed limit will increase accidents?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Rural highways have fewer pedestrians than urban streets.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Most drivers on rural highways are currently driving at speeds below 65 mph.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Accident rates correlate strongly with driver inattention rather than with the gap between posted and actual speeds.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Speed limit signs on rural highways are clearly visible and well-maintained.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Rural highways carry less traffic than interstate highways.

explanations.correct: The officials argue that higher speeds cause reduced attention and thus more accidents. Confirming that inattention (not gap-reduction) is the dominant causal factor in accidents strengthens their prediction that raising limits will increase accidents.
explanations.A: Pedestrian presence is not relevant to the speed-limit argument.
explanations.B: If drivers are already below 65, then raising the limit may not change actual speeds, which would weaken rather than strengthen the officials' prediction.
explanations.C: Correct. This confirms the mechanism by which speed increases lead to accidents.
explanations.D: Sign visibility doesn't address whether higher speeds cause more accidents.
explanations.E: Traffic volume is independent of the speed-safety relationship.

difficultyReason: Single-link causal argument in environmental science. The correct answer rules out a competing cause of the observed phenomenon.
stimulus: Biologists studying a forest noticed that the population of native songbirds has declined significantly over the past five years. They attribute this decline to invasive bird species that compete for nesting sites. An alternative explanation is that pesticide use in nearby agricultural areas has poisoned the songbirds' insect food sources.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the biologists' conclusion about the cause of the songbird decline?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Pesticide use in the agricultural areas near the forest has remained constant over the past decade.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Invasive bird species have historically been unsuccessful at establishing populations in temperate forests.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Native songbirds have adaptations that allow them to use alternative nesting sites.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Insect populations in the forest have remained stable over the past five years.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Native songbirds are an important part of the forest ecosystem.

explanations.correct: By confirming that insect populations—the songbirds' primary food source—have remained stable, this rules out the pesticide-poisoning alternative explanation. If food availability was unchanged, the decline must be due to another cause, namely competition from invasive species.
explanations.A: Constant pesticide use over a decade does not rule out whether it affected songbirds specifically in the past five years.
explanations.B: Historical failure does not explain why invasive species are suddenly present now.
explanations.C: Adaptability would not explain a sharp population decline.
explanations.D: Correct. This eliminates the food-source alternative.
explanations.E: Ecological importance is irrelevant to what caused the observed decline.

difficultyReason: Straightforward legal/ethics argument with a single obvious alternative cause. Correct answer rules it out by confirming an assumption.
stimulus: The defendant's fingerprints were found at the crime scene. The prosecutor argues this proves the defendant was present at the time of the crime. However, the defense attorney suggests that the fingerprints were planted by police during their investigation.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the prosecutor's argument that the defendant's presence is established by the fingerprints?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The defendant had a motive to commit the crime.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Police chain-of-custody procedures for evidence at the crime scene were strictly followed and documented.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The defendant had previously visited the location where the crime occurred.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Fingerprints can be obtained from many surfaces at a crime scene.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The defendant could not provide an alibi for the time of the crime.

explanations.correct: The defense suggests the fingerprints were planted. By confirming that chain-of-custody procedures were strictly followed, this rules out the planting explanation and strengthens the conclusion that the defendant's presence is evidenced by the fingerprints.
explanations.A: Motive supports guilt but not the specific claim that fingerprints prove presence.
explanations.B: Correct. This eliminates the planting alternative.
explanations.C: Prior visits are irrelevant to when these fingerprints were left.
explanations.D: Surface availability does not speak to whether these particular prints are genuine.
explanations.E: Lack of alibi supports guilt generally but doesn't address fingerprint authenticity.

difficultyReason: Simple linguistic/cognitive argument about learning. The correct answer confirms a key premise of the causal mechanism.
stimulus: Children who are read to frequently develop larger vocabularies than children who are rarely read to. This is probably because reading exposes children to a wider variety of words than everyday conversation does.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most supports the argument about the cause of vocabulary differences?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Parents who read to their children tend to have larger vocabularies themselves.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Books contain a greater diversity of word types and usage than occurs in typical spoken conversation.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Children who develop large vocabularies early tend to perform better academically.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Some children who are not read to still develop large vocabularies.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Reading ability and vocabulary size are correlated in adults.

explanations.correct: The argument proposes that reading causes larger vocabularies because books contain more diverse words than conversation. Confirming this premise—that books do indeed contain greater word diversity—strengthens the proposed mechanism.
explanations.A: Parents' own vocabularies might be a confound, not a confirmation of the reading mechanism.
explanations.B: Correct. This validates the key premise that books provide more word exposure.
explanations.C: Academic outcomes are irrelevant to why reading builds vocabulary.
explanations.D: Exceptions do not undermine a general causal claim.
explanations.E: Adult reading and vocabulary are outside the scope of the child-reading argument.

difficultyReason: Historical causal argument. The correct answer rules out a specific alternative explanation for an observed outcome.
stimulus: The Roman Empire's military declined in the fourth century. Historians argue that economic strain from defending vast borders drained resources needed for military maintenance and innovation. Others suggest the decline was simply due to the leadership of weak emperors.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the economic explanation for the military decline?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Several emperors in the fourth century were competent military strategists.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Tax revenues decreased significantly during the same period that military strength declined.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Weak leadership had occurred in earlier centuries without causing permanent military decline.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The Empire's borders were roughly the same in the fourth century as they had been in previous centuries.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Neighboring barbarian tribes possessed superior weaponry compared to Roman forces.

explanations.correct: By showing that weak leadership alone did not cause permanent decline in the past, this weakens the 'weak emperors' alternative and strengthens the case that economic factors were the distinguishing cause in the fourth century.
explanations.A: Competent emperors would support the leadership explanation, not weaken it.
explanations.B: While this shows a correlation, declining revenues themselves do not rule out leadership as the culprit.
explanations.C: Correct. This shows weak leadership is insufficient to cause permanent decline, supporting the economic explanation as the special factor in the fourth century.
explanations.D: Border stability would suggest defense costs stayed constant, which doesn't clarify causation.
explanations.E: Barbarian superiority would explain external military pressure but not the internal economic strain argument.

difficultyReason: Technology adoption argument with a single clear alternative. The correct answer confirms the causal mechanism.
stimulus: Sales of e-readers have increased dramatically in the past decade. Publishers believe this trend is driven by consumers' preference for the convenience of digital reading. However, critics argue the growth is instead due to aggressive marketing and price cuts by electronics retailers.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most strengthens the publishers' argument about consumer preference?

choices.label: A
choices.text: E-reader prices have remained relatively stable over the past five years.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Survey data shows that consumers cite convenience as the primary reason for choosing e-readers over print books.

choices.label: C
choices.text: E-reader battery life has improved significantly.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Advertising budgets for e-readers have increased substantially in recent years.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Print book sales have remained stable rather than declining sharply.

explanations.correct: The publishers claim that consumer preference for convenience drives sales. Direct evidence that consumers identify convenience as their primary purchase motivation strongly supports this causal claim.
explanations.A: Stable prices would actually undermine the marketing/price-cut alternative, but this is weaker than direct preference evidence.
explanations.B: Correct. This directly confirms that convenience preference is the stated reason for the purchase decision.
explanations.C: Battery improvements support that e-readers are convenient but don't rule out marketing as the driver.
explanations.D: Increased advertising strengthens the critics' marketing explanation, not the publishers'.
explanations.E: Stable print sales tell us nothing about why e-readers grew in preference.

difficultyReason: Arts/education causal argument with one obvious alternative. Correct answer rules out the competing explanation.
stimulus: An arts academy reports that students who participate in music training show higher academic achievement in math and science. The academy suggests that music training develops cognitive skills transferable to these subjects. A rival explanation is that only academically strong students choose to take music lessons.
questionStem: Which one of the following, if true, most supports the academy's causal claim about music training?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Students at the academy come from diverse socioeconomic backgrounds.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Music training was randomly assigned to some students while others received standard curriculum, and the trained group showed greater math and science gains.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Students who do well in music often do well in other subjects.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Music teachers at the academy hold advanced degrees in music.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The academy has been in operation for over twenty years.

explanations.correct: By showing that music training was randomly assigned—not chosen by pre-existing high-achievers—and that this group showed greater gains, this eliminates the selection-bias alternative. Random assignment proves the correlation is causal rather than due to self-selection.
explanations.A: Socioeconomic diversity is irrelevant to whether music causes academic gains.
explanations.B: Correct. Random assignment and subsequent gains rule out the self-selection alternative.
explanations.C: This correlation still allows for selection bias: strong students choose music and do well in other subjects.
explanations.D: Teacher qualifications don't address whether training causes the observed gains.
explanations.E: Institutional longevity is irrelevant to the causal mechanism.
